clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female with insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes presented to the ED with fever (39.3°C), lethargy, vomiting, lower back pain, flank pain, dysuria, urinary frequency, and malodorous urine. Physical examination revealed left lower quadrant tenderness and positive left-sided costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis showed pyuria (21-50 WBC/hpf) and small leukocyte esterase, consistent with upper urinary tract infection. Chest X-ray on admission demonstrated left lower lobe consolidation with pleural effusion, indicating systemic infection. During hospitalization, CT abdomen/pelvis revealed a left renal subcapsular hematoma measuring 3.8 x 5.4 x 8.3 cm. Urine culture grew Candida glabrata. Follow-up outpatient CT showed interval growth of the hematoma to 13.3 x 10.9 x 8.5 cm with gas foci, confirming infection. The patient was initially treated with empiric piperacillin/tazobactam; cultures subsequently grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, and antibiotics were narrowed to ceftriaxone based on susceptibility testing. A percutaneous drain was placed in the left renal abscess, draining approximately 500 mL of pus, with post-procedure CT showing near-complete resolution. Three-month follow-up renal ultrasound revealed complete resolution of perinephric and subcapsular fluid collections.

final.final_diagnosis: acute pyelonephritis secondary to an acute spontaneous idiopathic left renal subcapsular hematoma that became infected
final.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female with insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes presented to the ED with fever (39.3°C), lethargy, vomiting, lower back pain, flank pain, dysuria, urinary frequency, and malodorous urine. Physical examination revealed left lower quadrant tenderness and positive left-sided costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis showed pyuria (21-50 WBC/hpf) and small leukocyte esterase, consistent with upper urinary tract infection. Chest X-ray on admission demonstrated left lower lobe consolidation with pleural effusion, indicating systemic infection. During hospitalization, CT abdomen/pelvis revealed a left renal subcapsular hematoma measuring 3.8 x 5.4 x 8.3 cm. Urine culture grew Candida glabrata. Follow-up outpatient CT showed interval growth of the hematoma to 13.3 x 10.9 x 8.5 cm with gas foci, confirming infection. The patient was initially treated with empiric piperacillin/tazobactam; cultures subsequently grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, and antibiotics were narrowed to ceftriaxone based on susceptibility testing. A percutaneous drain was placed in the left renal abscess, draining approximately 500 mL of pus, with post-procedure CT showing near-complete resolution. Three-month follow-up renal ultrasound revealed complete resolution of perinephric and subcapsular fluid collections.
